threatBuild.notes: Casino manager. Not a fighter. His value is access and cooperation — and the standing rules he names tonight bind tomorrow.

scenes.hazards: None tonight. Tomorrow the casino opens.

options.label: Take Mandelbrot's briefing seriously and run final cover-checks
options.consequence: No friction tomorrow at door checks. Crew enters cleanly. Cover work compounds.

options.label: Skip the briefing — drink, gamble, blow off steam
options.consequence: No mechanical penalty, but the Mandelbrot rapport is colder when the Pressure Cooker scene needs it. Mandelbrot gratitude tier starts one rung lower.

narrativeLinks.note: The Assiduous arrival has been relocated to the new Day 2 scene (Message from the Banshee), where it lands inside the tournament alongside the Switch Dirty Money commit prompt.

encounters.name: Beat 1 — Final Pre-Tournament Prep
encounters.trigger: Evening before the tournament, casino entry checkpoints in twelve hours
encounters.description: The crew is at their lodgings or a quiet upper-level cafe running last-minute prep — cover identities, buy-in credits in the right pouches, weapons-permit discs for security PCs, the Switch-Moro line confirmed (or not). Varth runs a final intel sweep on Arandis, Lady Fioro, Silas Draver, and the cashier rotation. Maya runs diagnostics on the Banshee's exit vector. Everything is, briefly, going to plan.
encounters.tactics: NO DICE — orientation. End beat with the walk to the casino concourse.

encounters.name: Beat 2 — Mandelbrot's Standing-Rules Briefing
encounters.trigger: Crew assembles in the count-room office for the house briefing
encounters.description: Jacc Mandelbrot — Sullustan, sun-creased, the casino's house manager and head of the count room — runs through the standing rules in the flat tone of a man who has done this hundreds of times. (1) Every competitor wears a comm-jamming pin once seated. The pin produces a vocoder static field that kills any outgoing comlink signal from within five meters of the wearer. Removal of the pin while inside the casino is grounds for immediate expulsion and forfeit of buy-in. The pin can be spotted on a competitor by anyone watching for it (skulduggery or investigation, Resist 3) but spotting it does not let you defeat it; it only confirms what is in play. (2) Buy-back-in is permitted: when a competitor gets sick mid-round (it happens; the casino looks the other way as long as the paperwork is clean), an eliminated player can re-enter for a flat 2,000-credit fee paid to the cashier. Use it as the rescue valve. (3) Five named players are entered: Lt. Armen Arandis (Imperial cover, plays cold), Lady Mirana Fioro (Hapan, plays for keeps), Silas Draver (loud, drunk-acting, sober — Mandelbrot has already flagged him to floor security), Creeska (Rodian, two prior expulsions for card-marking on other circuits — watch him), and a Twi'lek named Koroma Moro who arrived alone and paid in marked Bespin chips. (4) Three exits from the casino floor — the velvet entrance, the service corridor that runs to the count room, and the upper-deck fire stair to the air-tram platform. Lockdown closes all three on the manager's call.
encounters.tactics: NO DICE — rules briefing. These are mechanics that bind tomorrow's scenes. End beat with Mandelbrot shaking each PC's hand and asking, politely, that they not embarrass him.

encounters.name: Beat 3 — One Quiet Round
encounters.trigger: After the briefing — crew has free time before standard daybreak
encounters.description: Twenty real minutes of unstructured RP. Crew may share a drink at the Banshee galley with Maya, take one walk around the upper Cloudscape promenade, or place one optional cantina conversation. No mandatory beat.
encounters.tactics: NO DICE — atmosphere. Honor whichever direction the players take it. End scene at standard daybreak; hand off to adv3-p2-s1 (Day 1 — Catch the Cheater).

environmentMechanics.name: Mandelbrot Rapport
environmentMechanics.effect: Mandelbrot starts at neutral. Crews who run Beat 2 attentively start at Mandelbrot Rapport tier 2 (free social win at adv3-p2-s3 Pressure Cooker if the Szygar incident is resolved quietly). Crews who skip the briefing start at tier 0.
environmentMechanics.mitigation: Show up to the briefing.

rewards.narrative: Tournament-eve prep complete. Standing rules briefed. The doors open at daybreak.

pacing.openingBeat: Final preparations the night before the tournament.
pacing.risingAction: Mandelbrot's standing-rules briefing — comm-jamming pin, buy-back-in, the five named players, the three exits.
pacing.resolution: The crew sleeps on what they know. Daybreak comes.

disciplineChallenges.context: Final cover-identity rehearsal with Maya before the casino doors open.

control.failure: Cover has a visible seam. Tomorrow at the entry checkpoint, the relevant entry-path check (Spectator bluff or Competitor identity verification) takes +1 Resist. Real friction at the door.
control.mastery: Cover is so polished that Mandelbrot's door staff treat the PC as a returning regular. -1 Resist on the entry-path check tomorrow.

effect.fleeting: Cover holds. No bonus, no penalty.
effect.masterful: Cover is clean. Tomorrow's entry check passes without friction.
effect.legendary: Cover is air-tight. Maya stops correcting and starts complimenting. The PC walks into the casino tomorrow as if they have always belonged there.

scenes.title: The Elimination Rounds — Day 1
scenes.subtitle: Day 1 — Catch the Cheater
scenes.readAloud:
The Royal Casino is a loud, smoky, aggressive establishment where prospectors gamble away fortunes and refugees bet their last credits. Over fifty competitors crowd the tables. The air is thick with Corellian whiskey, Ryll spice smoke, and the mechanical whir of shuffling droids.

Every seated competitor is wearing a small black pin on their lapel — Mandelbrot named it last night. The pin produces a vocoder static field; comlink chatter dies within five meters of any wearer. Whatever you need to pass to a teammate at the table today, you pass face-to-face during the breaks.

You notice four players worth watching: a flamboyant human named Silas Draver who seems drunk but isn't, a cold Hapan noblewoman named Lady Fioro who bankrupts a weeping Dug in the first hour, a Twi'lek named Koroma Moro who keeps to himself, and a Rodian named Creeska who is, even to a casual eye, doing something with his sleeve that he should not be doing.
scenes.gmNotes:
DAY 1 of the tournament. The headline beat is Catch the Cheater (security PC) / Make a Read (competitor PC) — Creeska, the Rodian, is palming a card-marker. The forcing function is Mandelbrot's tournament-administrator gavel at end of session: tables reset, half the field is eliminated by the cashier's posted bracket, downtime block follows, Day 2 opens fresh.

The comm-jamming pin is now LIVE for every competitor PC. Intel must be passed in person during break beats. Security PCs, spectator PCs, and the Banshee crew are the relays.

The Switch Dirty Money offer (if the crew accepted in principle in adv3-p1-s4) is in play but does not commit until Day 3 (adv3-p2-s3 Pressure Cooker). Switch may send a Day 1 reminder ping if the GM wants to keep the temptation visible — flagged in Beat 4 below.

npcs.name: Creeska
npcs.notes: Rodian, mid-stakes circuit washout. Two prior expulsions for card-marking. Currently palming a thumb-sized chemical marker that tags high-value cards for him as they pass through his hands.

passive.name: Sleight Hands
passive.description: Creeska's skulduggery is favored. Spotting his card-marker requires a skulduggery or investigation check vs Resist 3 (his Resist).

gambit.name: Slip the Marker
gambit.description: When Creeska is targeted by a spotting check, he may dump the marker into a passing drinks tray. The check still surfaces the suspicion, but no physical evidence is recovered. Mandelbrot will not act without evidence.

exploit.name: Witness Plant
exploit.trigger: A PC publicly accuses Creeska without spotting evidence first.
exploit.description: Creeska gestures at a paid Bothan in the crowd who corroborates that the PC has been hovering and acting suspiciously. Mandelbrot expels the PC instead.

threatBuild.notes: Not a combat threat. The threat is reputational — a public false accusation costs the accusing PC their seat. Spotting his marker first (skulduggery or investigation, Resist 3) gets him expelled cleanly and earns Mandelbrot Rapport +1.

npcs.name: Koroma Moro
npcs.notes: Twi'lek, mid-thirties, owns a single light freighter that Switch has been bankrolling since Switch's last Kessel-run debt collection went sideways. Moro plays a competent middle game and folds when he should. He is at the table because Switch put him there.

passive.name: Patient Player
passive.description: Moro will not act on a tip from the crew unless the tip is delivered face-to-face by a teammate in the crowd or by a spectator PC during a break. The comm-jamming pin makes electronic relay impossible.

exploit.name: Switch's Hand
exploit.trigger: The crew commits to the Dirty Money fork at the Day 3 commit point.
exploit.description: From that beat forward, Moro plays to a script the crew can shape — they may feed him reads, trigger distractions at competing tables, or actively cheat on his behalf (skulduggery vs Mandelbrot's house-floor Resist 4 — failure = expulsion).

threatBuild.notes: Linchpin of the Dirty Money fork. If Moro wins the Final Table, Switch pays the crew 5-7% of the pot (negotiable, top of the range if Moro wins clean) AND the Imperial card-arrangement transfer between Arandis and Fioro never happens. No 137.12. No Shackles of Nizon lead. The fork genuinely competes with the Imperial intel-grab.

npcs.name: Silas Draver
npcs.notes: Posing as a drunk gambler. Actually casing the room for a robbery.

npcEffects.legendary: Chassis damage + [Suppressed] + [Exposed]

maneuver.name: Reposition
maneuver.description: Modifies Move. Move up to 2 zones. If the Harrier ends farther from all enemies than it started, +1 Power on next attack.

gambit.name: Pinning Fire
gambit.description: In addition to normal effects, target gains [Slowed] Tactical.

exploit.name: Snap Shot
exploit.trigger: A PC uses Move to enter or cross a zone within weapon range.
exploit.description: Immediately attack that PC at -2 Power.

threatBuild.notes: The third-party wildcard. Agile: +1 Evasion. He's been planning this heist for months. The heroes don't see him coming.

npcs.name: Various Competitors
npcs.notes: Species with telepathy, cybernetic implants, alien poker faces.

passive.name: Background Noise
passive.description: Fifty competitors provide social cover. Heroes blend in.

threatBuild.notes: Color NPCs. Not individually important. Provide atmosphere and social cover.

scenes.hazards: Comm-jamming pins on every competitor (no electronic relay). Casino surveillance. Mandelbrot's house security on the floor.

decisionPoints.prompt: Key Decision: Day 1 — Catch the Cheater

options.label: Spot Creeska's marker quietly and hand the evidence to Mandelbrot
options.consequence: Mandelbrot Rapport +1. Creeska expelled clean. The Day 1 pulse closes with a small win and a friendly nod from house security.

options.label: Confront Creeska publicly without evidence
options.consequence: Creeska's witness plant flips the room. Accusing PC is expelled instead. Buy-back-in costs 2,000 credits to re-enter Day 2.

options.label: Ignore Creeska, focus on cards and reads
options.consequence: No Mandelbrot Rapport movement. Creeska remains in the field and can interfere with the Day 2 standings.

narrativeLinks.note: Entry-path menu — the four PC roles set up here are now live at the table.
Day 1 hands off to Day 2 (Message from the Banshee) at end of session.
The Switch Dirty Money commit point is Day 3 (Pressure Cooker). The pitch is in play here on Day 1; the lock-in waits.

encounters.name: Beat 1 — Reading the Floor
encounters.trigger: Crew enters the Royal Casino floor on Day 1
encounters.description: The first hour of the tournament is observation. Competitor PCs are seated at separate tables (per registration). Security PCs walk the floor on Mandelbrot's rota. Spectator PCs work the rail. The brief is to identify the players who matter: Arandis, Fioro, Draver, Creeska, Moro. Krygg's "plays like a man who has been told what to do with cards" tell from the Ugnaught conversation grants free identification of Arandis to any PC who heard it.
encounters.tactics: NO DICE for free identifications. Each PC may attempt one Sense (sense_spark) check per other named player to read deeper than the surface — Resist 3, failure = surface read only (no deeper detail). End beat after the first hour of observation.

encounters.name: Beat 2 — Catch the Cheater (security PC) / Make a Read (competitor PC)
encounters.trigger: Creeska palms his marker during a third-round hand
encounters.description: Creeska is cheating in plain sight. The marker is a thumb-sized chemical applicator that tags high-value cards as they pass through his hands. The tell is a single repeating motion — sleeve, thumb, deck, sleeve — that takes one observation pass to spot if you know what you are looking for. Security PCs can spot it on a skulduggery or investigation check (Resist 3) and hand the evidence to Mandelbrot for a clean expulsion (Mandelbrot Rapport +1). Competitor PCs at Creeska's table can spot it from across the felt on the same check (skulduggery or investigation, Resist 3) and use it to fold strategically against him without triggering a reaction. The CRITICAL trap: if a PC accuses Creeska publicly without first surfacing the marker as evidence, Creeska's pre-paid Bothan witness corroborates that the accusing PC has been hovering and acting suspiciously, and Mandelbrot expels the accuser instead.
encounters.tactics: ROLL — skulduggery or investigation vs Resist 3. SUCCESS: marker spotted, evidence in hand, Creeska expelled, Mandelbrot Rapport +1. FAILURE: PC reads Creeska as merely twitchy, no evidence, no movement. CRITICAL FAILURE PATH: PC who accuses Creeska without spotting the marker first is expelled by the Bothan witness plant. Buy-back-in costs 2,000 credits to re-enter Day 2.

encounters.name: Beat 3 — Day One Card Play
encounters.trigger: First competitive session of the tournament
encounters.description: Sabacc is played. Each competitor PC plays through six hands at their assigned table while wearing the comm-jamming pin. The cards themselves matter less than the social tells — bluffs that match cover identity, betting patterns consistent with the brag-and-price the Ugnaughts coached, and the absence of crew-level coordination (no eye contact across tables, no shared bathroom breaks). The pin actively prevents crew comlink relay, so competitor PCs operate solo at the felt unless a security or spectator PC physically walks up and passes a note during a posted break.
encounters.tactics: RUN: Charm or Deception vs Resist 3 per competitor PC for cover-hold under live pressure. Failure = cover slips, +1 Resist on the next Charm/Deception check at the table that day. Each PC who survives Day 1 advances to Day 2; each PC who busts is eliminated and must spend the 2,000-credit buy-back-in fee to re-enter on Day 2 (otherwise drops to spectator role for the rest of the tournament).

encounters.name: Beat 4 — Day One Recess at the Back Bar (and Switch's Reminder)
encounters.trigger: Tournament adjourns for evening recess
encounters.description: The casino's back bar — open only to registered players and their plus-ones — fills up. PCs may approach Lt. Arandis (drinks alone, badly), Lady Fioro (holds court with a small Hapan retinue, watches Arandis from across the room), Silas Draver (genuinely drunk now, having dropped the act), or Koroma Moro (sits alone at a corner table with a Twi'lek liqueur and a private comlink). Switch may send a private Day 1 reminder to any crewmember who took the Dirty Money offer in principle — a one-line ping confirming Moro is at the corner table and the Day 3 commit window opens after the Maya/Varth argument.
encounters.tactics: RUN: Charm / Sense (sense_spark) / Persuasion vs Resist 3 per contact. Each contact yields one named piece of intel that pays off in adv3-p2-s2 through adv3-p2-s4 (Arandis: the exact wafer hand-off timing; Fioro: Varga's docking bay number; Draver: a half-formed heist diversion the crew can co-opt; Moro: confirmation of the Switch arrangement and his asking-price for the win). End beat at last call. Comm-jamming pins come off at the bar — comlinks work here.

encounters.name: Beat 5 — Day One Closes
encounters.trigger: Mandelbrot's tournament administrator calls Day 1 at midnight standard
encounters.description: The administrator gavels Day 1 closed. The cashier posts the Day 2 bracket on the casino's marquee — half the field eliminated, the surviving PCs and named players advanced. Eliminated PCs are notified and given the 2,000-credit buy-back-in chip if they want it. Tables reset for the morning. The crew has a downtime block before Day 2 opens.
encounters.tactics: NO DICE — forcing function. This is the Day 1 -> Day 2 transition. Note the surviving cast on the bracket; eliminated PCs decide on the buy-back-in. End scene; hand off to adv3-p2-s2 (Day 2 — Message from the Banshee).

environmentMechanics.name: Comm-Jamming Pin (Active on Competitors)
environmentMechanics.trigger: When a competitor PC is seated at a tournament table
environmentMechanics.effect: Every seated competitor wears a small black lapel pin issued by the house. The pin produces a vocoder static field that kills any outgoing comlink signal from within five meters of the wearer. Competitor PCs cannot use comlinks during play. Spotting the pin on another competitor (to confirm what is in play, not to defeat it) requires a skulduggery or investigation check vs Resist 3 — failure on this spotting check means the PC tries to comlink during the table and gets caught by the floor manager (Mandelbrot Rapport -1, public warning). Removing or disabling the pin while inside the casino is grounds for immediate expulsion and forfeit of buy-in. The pin comes off naturally at the back bar (Beat 4) and at all posted breaks.
environmentMechanics.mitigation: Use security and spectator PCs as meatspace intel-relays. Pass notes, hand signals, drink-tray drops during breaks. Do not try to defeat the pin.

environmentMechanics.name: Buy-Back-In (2,000 credits)
environmentMechanics.trigger: When a competitor PC is eliminated mid-round and a competitor "gets sick"
environmentMechanics.effect: An eliminated PC may re-enter the tournament for a flat 2,000-credit fee paid to the cashier when a competitor at any table withdraws under medical or personal pretext. The fee is non-negotiable and the slot is first-come; if more PCs than open slots want to re-enter, the GM picks based on table fiction. Use the buy-back-in as the rescue valve to keep eliminated players in the scene.
environmentMechanics.mitigation: Pay the 2,000 and re-enter. Track the credit cost on the crew sheet.

environmentMechanics.name: Tournament Administrator (Forcing Function)
environmentMechanics.effect: Mandelbrot's tournament administrator gavels the day closed. The cashier posts the Day 2 bracket. Tables reset for the morning. The crew has a downtime block before Day 2 opens.
environmentMechanics.mitigation: N/A — this is the time-passes mechanic that hands off to adv3-p2-s2.

rewards.narrative: Day 1 closes. Half the field is eliminated. The crew's competitor PCs (or buy-back-in survivors) advance to Day 2. Creeska is either expelled or still in play depending on how the cheat-catch beat resolved.

pacing.openingBeat: Doors open. Comm-jamming pins go on. Five named players to read.
pacing.risingAction: The Catch the Cheater beat — Creeska palms his marker.
pacing.climax: Day 1 cards play out. Cover identities hold or slip.
pacing.resolution: Back-bar recess. Switch reminder. Mandelbrot gavels Day 1 closed.

disciplineChallenges.context: Spotting Creeska's card-marker from the table or the security floor.

control.failure: You read Creeska as merely twitchy. No marker spotted, no evidence in hand. If you publicly accuse him now, his Bothan witness flips the room and you are expelled instead.
control.mastery: Marker spotted AND you trace the chemical signature back to a Pyke supplier — leverage on Creeska that Mandelbrot can use across multiple casinos. Mandelbrot Rapport +2.

effect.fleeting: You catch the sleeve-thumb-deck-sleeve motion once. Enough to know what to look for next pass; not enough for evidence yet. One more observation round.
effect.masterful: Marker confirmed and the motion is unambiguous. Quietly hand the evidence to Mandelbrot. Creeska is expelled clean. Mandelbrot Rapport +1.
effect.legendary: Marker spotted, the chemical applicator is photographed mid-application, and the evidence is in Mandelbrot's hand within sixty seconds. Creeska is led out the service exit before he knows he has been seen. Mandelbrot Rapport +2.

disciplineChallenges.context: Watching Creeska from the rail (security or spectator PC).

control.failure: Crowd noise, cigarra smoke, table angles — you cannot get a clean line on his hands. No marker spotted. Public accusation now will trigger the witness plant.
control.mastery: Marker spotted AND you read the cover the Bothan witness is providing. You can intercept the Bothan and offer your own counter-bribe before Creeska deploys him.

effect.fleeting: You catch one motion. Plausible suspicion; not yet evidence. Watch one more pass.
effect.masterful: Marker confirmed. Hand the read to a security PC or pass it to Mandelbrot directly. Creeska expelled clean. Mandelbrot Rapport +1.
effect.legendary: Marker confirmed and the Bothan witness is identified before Creeska can deploy him. Mandelbrot Rapport +1, and the Bothan owes you a favor.

disciplineChallenges.context: Holding cover under live tournament pressure (competitor PC).

control.failure: Cover slips. +1 Resist on the next Charm or Deception check at the table today. An observant opponent files the read away for Day 2.
control.mastery: Cover is so polished other players defer. -1 Resist on all Charm/Deception checks at the table for the rest of Day 1.

effect.fleeting: Cover holds. Six hands played. You advance to Day 2 with a thin reputation.
effect.masterful: Cover holds clean. Six hands played. You advance with a respectable reputation and one named opponent who wants to play you again tomorrow.
effect.legendary: You become a story at the rail. Bothans are betting on you to make Day 3. Two named opponents specifically request your table assignment for Day 2.

disciplineChallenges.context: Reading Koroma Moro at the back bar — is he Switch's man as advertised, or is there a wrinkle?

control.failure: You read Moro as a competent middle-stakes captain who is playing his own game. The Switch arrangement does not register on him. (If Switch did pitch the crew, the GM may use this miss to plant doubt — is Switch lying about Moro, or is Moro lying to Switch?)
control.mastery: Full read AND you confirm the Kessel-run debt detail Switch named — Moro owes Switch a freighter's worth and is at the table to clear it. The arrangement is exactly what Switch said.

effect.fleeting: Moro is a patient player carrying weight. Plausible match for Switch's description; not yet confirmed.
effect.masterful: Moro is Switch's man. The body language matches the pitch. The arrangement is real and Moro is committed.
effect.legendary: Full psychological read: Moro is a captain who lost his ship to a debt, is at the table to win it back, and would rather not cheat — but will, if the crew gives him the cover for it.

scenes.title: The Elimination Rounds — Day 2
scenes.subtitle: Day 2 — Message from the Banshee
scenes.readAloud:
Daybreak. The casino doors open on a thinned field — half the names from yesterday are gone, and the surviving competitors look it. Coffee. Black. Comm-jamming pins on. Tables reset.

You are an hour into the second session when Varth's voice cuts in over the crew's open channel — the spectator and security PCs hear it first; the competitor PCs at the felt do not, because the pin is doing its job.

"We have a problem. A massive energy spike just hit the system edge. An Imperial Star Destroyer just dropped out of hyperspace. It is the Assiduous — Inquisitor Draco's flagship."

A beat of silence on the comm.

"That ship is the clean-up crew. If Arandis loses the money wrong, or if Varga double-crosses them, Draco won't bother with arrests. He'll glass the city to bury the evidence. Pass that to whoever you have at a table. Quietly."
scenes.gmNotes:
DAY 2 of the tournament. The headline beat is Message from the Banshee — the Assiduous arrival lands here, mid-tournament, instead of pre-tournament. The relay problem is the whole point: the news comes in over comlink, and the competitor PCs cannot hear it because the comm-jamming pin is on. The spectator/security PCs (or Maya/Varth on the Banshee) must walk it to the table during a posted break.

The Day 2 commit-prompt for the Switch Dirty Money fork is here too — Switch sends his second comm with the same offer and a request for an answer in principle, knowing the crew's actual lock-in is Day 3.

The Day 2 -> Day 3 transition hands cleanly into adv3-p2-s3 (Pressure Cooker, Day 3 morning Maya/Varth argument). Mandelbrot gavels Day 2 closed at midnight; the bracket narrows to twenty-four players; the surviving PCs advance to the Day 3 morning beat.

npcs.name: Inquisitor Valin Draco
npcs.notes: Aboard the Assiduous in orbit. Prepared to glass Cloud City if needed. NOT meant to be fought at this tier; he is an orbital threat whose presence is a clock, not an encounter.

npcEffects.legendary: Chassis damage + [Suppressed] + Controller's zone becomes [Hazard 1] until end of next round

maneuver.name: Overwatch Position
maneuver.description: Modifies Overwatch. Declare a zone. Any PC that enters, leaves, or takes an action in that zone presents an Opening AND gains [Suppressed].

gambit.name: Disrupt
gambit.description: In addition to normal effects, target gains [Stunned] Tactical. Target Steps Down the Control Die on all rolls until cleared.

exploit.name: Denial Fire
exploit.trigger: A PC enters a zone the Controller has declared as Overwatch.
exploit.description: Immediately attack that PC at -2 Power.

threatBuild.notes: Campaign nemesis. Power 7 vs PC tier — direct engagement is lethal. He is the reason to run, not the fight to win.

npcs.name: Switch (Twi'lek Information Broker — Remote)
npcs.notes: On a private comm from his suite somewhere in the upper Cloudscape. Pitches the Day 2 reminder of the Dirty Money offer. Not at the casino, not in the scene physically.

passive.name: Information Is Currency
passive.description: Switch never bluffs about what he knows. If he names a price (5-7% of Moro's pot), it is the real number.

threatBuild.notes: Remote contact. The relevant mechanic is the offer itself — see the Switch Day 2 reminder beat below.

scenes.hazards: Comm-jamming pins still active on competitors. The Assiduous is now in orbit. Mandelbrot has not yet been told the Star Destroyer is significant, but he will hear about it before Day 3.

decisionPoints.prompt: Key Decision: Day 2 — Message from the Banshee

options.label: Get the Assiduous news to the competitor PCs at the felt during the next break
options.consequence: The crew operates on shared knowledge from here on. Competitor PCs play the rest of Day 2 with the orbital threat in mind. Tone shifts.

options.label: Sit on the news; let the competitor PCs play clean and brief them at end-of-day
options.consequence: Competitor PCs miss the live pressure. The Day 3 morning Maya/Varth argument lands harder because they walk into it cold.

options.label: Accept Switch's reminder and signal commit to the Dirty Money fork in principle
options.consequence: Switch keeps Moro at the table. The Day 3 commit-window opens after the Maya/Varth argument. Imperial intel-grab is now genuinely in jeopardy.

options.label: Refuse Switch's reminder
options.consequence: Switch acknowledges and disengages. Moro plays his own game from here on. The Imperial card-arrangement transfer happens normally at the Final Table.

narrativeLinks.note: The Assiduous arrival originally lived in adv3-p1-s5 (Buy-In). It has been relocated here so it lands inside the tournament with the Switch commit prompt.
Day 2 hands off to Day 3 (Pressure Cooker / Maya-Varth argument) at end of session. The Switch commit window opens there.

encounters.name: Beat 1 — Day 2 Opens
encounters.trigger: Casino doors open Day 2 morning
encounters.description: Half the field is gone from yesterday. The surviving competitors look it. Coffee. Black. Comm-jamming pins on. Tables reset. First session of the day runs an hour before the Banshee comm cuts in.
encounters.tactics: NO DICE — atmosphere. The competitor PCs play one quiet hour of cards before Beat 2.

encounters.name: Beat 2 — Message from the Banshee (Assiduous Arrival)
encounters.trigger: Varth's voice cuts in over the crew's open channel one hour into the session
encounters.description: Varth's voice is genuinely afraid — the first time the crew has heard real fear in him since the Vanishing Place. He reports the Assiduous has dropped out of hyperspace and Inquisitor Draco is aboard. The competitor PCs at the felt cannot hear the comm because of the pin. The spectator/security PCs hear it first and must walk the news to the table during the next posted break — five real minutes of in-character improvisation in a casino full of people who are watching everything.
encounters.tactics: NO DICE for the comm itself. ROLL once if a PC tries to relay during play (skulduggery vs Resist 3 to pass a coded note across the felt without a floor manager noticing — failure = floor manager warning, Mandelbrot Rapport -1). Force-sensitive PCs may roll a free Sense (sense_spark) at advantage (sense_spark, no Resist) to confirm what they already know — Draco himself is aboard. End beat after the relay lands or fails.

encounters.name: Beat 3 — Switch's Day Two Reminder
encounters.trigger: During the same break window, if the Dirty Money offer was accepted in principle (or pitched and deferred) in adv3-p1-s4
encounters.description: Switch comms whichever crewmember answered the Day 1 pitch. He keeps it short: he wants confirmation that the offer is still live. He notes that Moro is holding the table well and could be in the final eight by end of Day 2. He is not pressuring; he is asking for an answer in principle so he knows whether to keep Moro at the felt. The actual commit is Day 3 (after the Maya/Varth argument in adv3-p2-s3).
encounters.tactics: NO DICE — pitch reminder. If the crew commits in principle, Moro plays to script from here. If the crew defers, Switch waits until Day 3 commit window. scenes.title: The Pressure Cooker
scenes.subtitle: Day 3
scenes.readAloud:
Before the tables open on Day 3, you catch Maya and Varth in a hushed argument near the docking bay. Maya's voice is low but furious:

"There are people on that ship, Varth. Living people in slave circuits. We have the datapad. We know where the Shackles of Nizon docks. We could —"

Varth cuts her off, cold and final: "That is not why we are here. We are here for the money. A rescue operation against an Imperial slave transport is suicide, and I will not risk this crew on your conscience."

Maya stares at him. Then she walks away without another word.

Day three. Only two tables remain. The buy-ins have escalated, and the audience has shifted from celebration to funeral silence.

Midway through the session, a Devaronian gambler named Szygar goes bust against Arandis. He snaps, leaping up and screaming accusations of cheating. A hold-out blaster appears in his hand.

Panic ripples through the crowd. Arandis doesn't flinch.
scenes.gmNotes:
OPENING BEAT: The heroes overhear Maya and Varth arguing about the Shackles of Nizon slave transport (from the Trandoshan datapad in Part 1). Maya wants to intervene and free the slaves. Varth shuts her down — too risky, not the mission. This is critical foreshadowing: Maya cares enough to act. When she later goes to the slave ship on her own and Varth conveniently never tells the crew, the players will remember this moment and understand what he allowed to happen.

The Szygar incident is a test for the heroes. If working security, they must subdue him without causing a casino shutdown. If playing, they must decide whether to intervene. If heroes don't act, Arandis's undercover Stormtroopers will vaporize Szygar, potentially causing a police investigation that cancels the tournament. Varth: 'Don't let them shoot! If the cops shut us down, we lose the money!' Success earns trust from casino owner Jacc Mandelbrot.

scenes.title: The Final Table
scenes.subtitle: Day 4
scenes.readAloud:
The final day. Five players remain under a harsh spotlight: Arandis, Fioro, Draver, the Rodian Creeska, and you.

Arandis plays strangely — folding strong hands against everyone except Fioro. He goes All In against her. She calls.

He reveals a losing hand. The crowd erupts. But instead of sweeping his cards away, Arandis deliberately arranges them on the table: One of Coins. Three of Sabers. Seven of Flasks.

Varth decodes it instantly: "1-3-7. That's a frequency — 137.12. It's the slave circuit control code for the Shackles of Nizon. He just handed her the keys to the getaway car AND the money."
scenes.gmNotes:
The climax of the game. Two outcomes — choose at the table based on whether the crew committed to the Switch Dirty Money fork at the Day 3 commit point in adv3-p2-s3.

[OUTCOME A — IMPERIAL FORK (default).] Arandis deliberately loses the massive pot to Fioro (Varga's proxy), transferring the Imperial payment. The card arrangement is a code — the slave circuit frequency for the Shackles of Nizon (137.12). Fioro now has the credits (digitally transferred to a datapad) and the ship code. The heroes must grab her before she leaves. The heist (adv3-p2-s5) and the Adv3 Part 3 sequence proceed with the Shackles lead intact.

[OUTCOME B — DIRTY MONEY FORK.] The crew is actively helping Moro win. The Imperial card-arrangement transfer NEVER HAPPENS — Arandis cannot maneuver Fioro into the winning seat because Moro keeps taking the pots Arandis needs to feed her. Fioro never receives the wafer. There is NO 137.12 frequency. There is NO Shackles of Nizon lead. Switch pays the crew 5-7% of Moro's pot. Mandelbrot Rapport may shift depending on whether the crew's table-side cheating got noticed (skulduggery vs Resist 4 — failure = expulsion).

Wire the chosen outcome through to adv3-p3-s1 (Gauntlet) and downstream. The Part 3 entry conditions for the heist sequence change: under Outcome A, the crew chases Fioro and the wafer toward the Shackles; under Outcome B, the crew chases Moro's payout and the Imperial payment vanishes into Varga's shell network entirely.

scenes.title: The Heist
scenes.subtitle: Combat
scenes.readAloud:
Just as you move to intercept Fioro, Silas Draver makes his play. He stands, pulls a heavy blaster, and fires into the ceiling.

"Nobody moves! The Empire isn't the only one getting paid today!"

The dealer droids spin around, revealing hidden blaster cannons. Draver's men — disguised as waiters and guests — pull weapons and secure the exits. Draver grabs Fioro, pressing a blaster to her temple.

"The datapad. Now."
scenes.gmNotes: Three-way crossfire in a crowded casino. Draver weaponized the dealer droids and planted his men as staff. The heroes are caught between Draver's heist crew, panicking civilians, and Arandis who draws a concealed military blaster to protect the transaction's secrecy. Arandis likely dies in the crossfire, removing the Imperial witness. Varth: 'Forget the civilians! Get the datapad!' After defeating Draver, Fioro spills Varga's location: Docking Bay 4414.

encounters.name: Beat 1 — The Casino in Ruins
encounters.trigger: Immediately after the s4 heist resolution
encounters.description: The Royal Casino floor is a wreck. Smoke from a discharged blaster hangs in the upper rafters. Two croupier droids are face-down. A Twi'lek dealer is trying to comfort a sobbing Bothan player. Sirens — Wing Guard responding — are audible from the upper concourse and closing fast. Lady Fioro is on the floor against the cashier counter, wounded in the thigh, blood pooling, terrified. She is talking. She will not stop talking. The crew has perhaps four minutes before Wing Guard arrives in force.
encounters.tactics: NO DICE — orientation. Establish urgency through ambient detail (the sirens, the Bothan crying, the smoke). Players orient themselves and choose a direction — Fioro is the obvious draw but PCs may also want to grab the wafer from the cashier counter if it was not yet taken in s4. End beat when a PC kneels beside Fioro to listen.

encounters.name: Beat 2 — Fioro Spills
encounters.trigger: PC engages with Fioro
encounters.description: Fioro, frightened and bleeding, gives up everything in a rush: "He's at the lower docks — Docking Bay 4414. He has the Shackles of Nizon holding in orbit on slave circuits. He's taking the gas and the slaves and leaving the sector tonight! I was supposed to be on that ship. He promised me passage. He is not going to keep that promise. Get him. Get him for me." She thrusts her data-bracelet at the nearest PC — it contains the bay's service-entry codes she was supposed to use to board.
encounters.tactics: NO DICE — Fioro talks willingly, terrified by the shooting and abandoned by Varga. Insight check (free) on Fioro: she is telling the truth and she is also planning to vanish off-world the moment Wing Guard distracts the crew. Players may choose to detain her (Wing Guard will find her, she will be charged, she will testify against Varga) or to let her run (she vanishes from the campaign — possibly returning later as a Hapan noble plot in a sequel). The data-bracelet is the deliverable either way.

encounters.name: Beat 3 — Varth's Grim Update
encounters.trigger: On the comm, in parallel with Fioro
encounters.description: Varth's voice cuts through the cashier-counter chaos: "The Shackles just activated its engines. Ten minutes to launch window. And — damn it. The Assiduous has moved. Geosynchronous over Cloud City. Not over the docks. Over the city. Draco is positioning to sterilize if Varga gets clear. We have ten minutes to put hands on Varga or this whole platform is glass." A beat. "Maya is spinning the Banshee up. We have an exit. We do not have a city after this. Move."
encounters.tactics: NO DICE — stakes escalation. Varth's update lands the actual cost of failure: Cloud City's population — millions — is leverage now. The ten-minute clock from this beat carries through s2-s3 (next adventure scenes). Players who heard the Storyteller's "the cost of the gift" or Krygg's Nuvo story should feel the moral weight of "we leave or millions burn" landing on the same nerve.

encounters.name: Beat 4 — Out the Service Corridor
encounters.trigger: Wing Guard reaches the casino floor
encounters.description: The crew runs. The casino service corridor — accessible via the Ugnaught keycard if it was earned in adv3-p1-s2 — empties into the lower platform tram station. From there it is six minutes to the lower industrial docks and Bay 4414. Without the keycard, the crew has to fight or talk past two Wing Guard checkpoints, costing two minutes of their ten-minute window. With the Ugnaught safe-house promise from Beat 4 of the s2 conversation, they may stash any wounded crew at the level 312 cantina and pick them up after — Krygg is there cooking the meal he promised.
encounters.tactics: RUN: Stealth / Athletics / fast-talk depending on route. With keycard: clean run, six minutes to docks. Without keycard: 2 checkpoints (Resist 2 each) and a +2 minute penalty per failed check. With safe-house: wounded PCs evacuate to level 312 and continue the next adventure with Krygg's (bad) hot meal already in their stomachs. End scene at the lower docks tram exit.

encounters.name: Beat 5 — Hand-off to Part 3
encounters.trigger: Crew arrives at lower industrial docks tram exit
encounters.description: The crew steps off the tram into the lower industrial docks — sodium-orange light, freight haulers, and Docking Bay 4414 visible four hundred meters across the platform, blast doors half-open, Varga's cargo train already moving toward the Shackles of Nizon's loading ramp. The Banshee is in low orbit per Maya's plan, ready to extract on signal. The Assiduous is a black wedge in the upper sky. The clock — eight minutes remaining of the ten Varth named — is on every visible chronometer in the dock yard.
encounters.tactics: NO DICE — handoff beat. Establishes the geography for adv3-p3-s1 (The Gauntlet) and the eight-minute remaining clock. Players may take one short prep action here (a final comm to Varth, a quick gear check, a moment with Maya on intercom). End the scene the moment a PC commits to the dock approach. Adventure 3 Part 3 begins.

The journey to the lower docks is a sprint through a city in lockdown. Varga has bribed the Wing Guard to declare you 'Enemy Saboteurs.'

The chase transitions from pristine white corridors into the steam-filled, rusted catwalks of the Industrial District. Tibanna gas vents hiss, obscuring vision, and the orange glow of the Bespin sunset filters through heavy industrial grates.

Running battle through Cloud City. The heroes are pinned down by corrupt Wing Guard and Stormtroopers. This is a chase — stopping to fight every enemy means being overwhelmed. Use the environment: shoot steam pipes to scald pursuers, jump onto moving cargo skiffs, cut through maintenance ducts. Varth acts as 'The Man in the Chair,' hacking door controls.

[OUTCOME A — IMPERIAL FORK (default).] The crew is chasing Fioro toward the air-tram with the 137.12 frequency wafer in her datapad. The Shackles of Nizon lead is intact and feeds the Part 3 sequence as written. The Wing Guard pursuit is hunting the wafer.

[OUTCOME B — DIRTY MONEY FORK.] No wafer changed hands. Fioro is still at the casino arguing with Varga's on-floor handler about a payment that never arrived. The Wing Guard pursuit was scrambled by Varga's payroll regardless — Varga is furious that the Imperial money is gone — so the chase still happens, but the prize is the Switch payout, not the Shackles intel. Adv3 Part 3 downstream scenes (Hutt's Hangar, Firefight, Grand Theft Starship, Skirmish Over Bespin, The Choice) proceed without the Shackles lead. scenes.title: Hutt's Hangar
scenes.subtitle: Docking Bay 4414
scenes.readAloud:
You kick open the blast doors to Docking Bay 4414. The cavernous hangar is open to the roiling clouds of Bespin on one side, wind howling through the magnetic field.

At the far north end, framed by heavy durasteel scaffolding, the Glorious Chariot squats in her launch cradle — gold and purple, three thruster housings visible through the scaffold gaps, turbines already cycling with a whine that climbs toward takeoff pitch. Between the two tallest scaffold towers, the yacht's boarding ramp is still down.

Six Z-95 Headhunters line the hangar walls — two along the port side, four along the starboard, nose-out toward the center. The rearmost crimson-trimmed fighter on the starboard line carries a Huttese glyph on the fuselage — Varga's stable. Pilots are already sprinting the open floor toward their cockpits, ladders down, engines cycling. Stacked cargo crates clutter the center of the bay — Trandoshan manifests, Guild Tibanna-gas hazard placards, still warm from the offload.

Varga's voice booms from the cradle's loudspeakers, fat with panic. When a cradle monitor cuts to a live feed, he sees you. Fear becomes rage.

"Kill them! They brought the Inquisitor down on us! I want their heads! Get me in the air NOW!"
scenes.gmNotes:
The final confrontation with Varga. The Glorious Chariot sits in the adjacent launch cradle at the NORTH end of the map, her thrusters visible through the scaffolding, boarding ramp still down between the scaffold towers. Six Z-95 Headhunters line the hangar walls (2 port, 4 starboard) and their pilots are racing the open floor toward cockpits.

THE LAUNCH CLOCK: The Chariot is priming for launch. Track it as 6 beats. Each beat is one round of the fight. When the clock hits zero, the Chariot lifts and the scene transitions into s3 (Firefight — closing the hangar) and then s4/s5 (Grand Theft Starship + Skirmish Over Bespin — pursuit in orbit). The Chariot leaving is a BAD outcome but not a fail state — it's the 'normal' path and the pursuit is the planned finale. Stopping the Chariot before launch is the HARD path.

TWO WIN CONDITIONS, TWO PATHS:
1. STOP THE CHARIOT (hard): Heroes must reach the Launch Cradle zone at the north end before beat 6. Options once there — (a) ascend the ramp and fight Varga aboard the yacht (his bulk is a weapon in the narrow corridors — use the ramp/airlock as a choke point), (b) sabotage the visible thruster housings from the scaffolding (Tech check, Hard — successful disable locks the Chariot on the pad), (c) trigger the Tibanna-gas cargo crates as a chained detonation that cracks the cradle mounts (requires reaching the crates AND igniting them while heroes have already moved north — high risk). If heroes pull any of these off, Varga is trapped — boss fight on his terms, but he can't flee.
2. LET THE CHARIOT LAUNCH (normal): Heroes steal a Z-95 from the walls and chase the yacht into Bespin's atmosphere (s4 → s5). This is the designed through-line. The hangar fight becomes a sprint to a cockpit rather than an assault on the ramp.

PILOT INTERCEPT ECONOMY: Each Z-95 pilot that reaches a cockpit and launches = one additional harrier in s5. Shooting pilots on the ladders is high-value. Make this explicit to the table.

SCAFFOLDING: Climbable with Athletics. Ascending the scaffold opens a sightline to the cradle AND a path to the ramp. BUT when the Chariot's engines reach full cycle (beat 4+), heat wash makes the scaffolding impassable. Audibility in the north half of the hangar drops to zero — shouted coordination fails on beat 4+.

VARGA'S POSITION: On the Chariot's bridge or at the top of the ramp. NOT on the hangar floor. Heroes who want to engage Varga directly MUST climb the scaffolding or push up the ramp. He shouts commands and taunts via the cradle PA; the scene's emotional presence is his voice in the hangar, his physical presence one zone away behind the scaffold.

CARGO CRATE HAZARD: The center-floor crate cluster is Guild-marked Tibanna gas. Sustained fire or a deliberate ignition check triggers an area detonation — [Concealment] smoke wall for 2 beats, damage to anyone adjacent, and if heroes position it right, the blast cracks the cradle mount scaffolding. High-risk, high-reward environmental play.

[OUTCOME GATE — wire from adv3-p2-s4 (Final Table).]
[OUTCOME A — IMPERIAL FORK (default).] Fioro's wafer carries the 137.12 Shackles of Nizon frequency. The crew is hunting/holding/escaping with the Shackles lead intact; this scene runs as written.
[OUTCOME B — DIRTY MONEY FORK.] Moro won the Final Table. No wafer transferred. No 137.12 frequency. The chase/firefight/escape still happens (Varga is enraged the Imperial money never landed and his Wing Guard payroll is still pursuing the crew), but the prize at the end of this scene is the Switch payout (5-7% of Moro's pot), NOT Shackles intel. Where this scene's text references the wafer/frequency/Shackles, treat those references as the Switch payout chips and Moro's extraction.

tacticalMap.gmTacticalNotes:
FOCAL ZONES: Cargo Crates (primary cover cluster), Starboard Fighter Line (four Z-95s including Varga's crimson personal craft), and Hangar Floor (deadly open ground connecting them).

HERO ENTRY: Hangar Entrance (south). The crew rolls in hot from the Gauntlet (s1) and must decide in the first beat: push straight up the floor (fastest, fully exposed), hug the port fighter line (cover but bypassed by starboard fire), or make the cargo crate cluster (primary cover but a pilot scramble race).

VARGA'S PILOTS: Mercenary pilots sprint from the starboard entrance (or were already in the Starboard Fighter Line) toward their Z-95 cockpits. Each Z-95 that launches = one TIE-equivalent harrier in s5 (Skirmish Over Bespin). Grounding pilots on the deck in s2 directly reduces the swarm size in s5. Make this explicit to the table — every shot that drops a scrambling pilot is a fighter that doesn't launch.

VARGA'S PERSONAL Z-95: Rearmost fighter in the Starboard Fighter Line. Crimson detailing, Huttese glyph on fuselage. If heroes want to STEAL a ship for the s4 'Grand Theft Starship' beat, this is the prestige target — fully fueled, hot-swap ready, Varga's own. Alternative: any of the other Z-95s works, but taking Varga's specifically has downstream narrative weight (Varga screams about it on comms, adds +1 to Grief pool in s6).

REAR EXHAUST HAZARD: Rear Exhaust Wall vents cycle every 2 beats. PCs or NPCs in the zone when vents fire take flue-gas damage AND audibility drops to zero — shouted coordination fails for one beat. Good for narrative swings when a pilot tries to reach a Z-95 by running the rear.

CARGO CRATE FIRE RISK: Crates are Guild-marked Tibanna gas. A stray sustained-fire hit OR a deliberate tech/ranged check can ignite one — area explosion, [Concealment] smoke wall for 2 beats, random damage to anyone adjacent. Table should know the crates are volatile before they take cover there. Mercenary fire will eventually ignite them if the fight drags — use this as a clock.

LOCKDOWN PANEL: Hangar Entrance has an emergency lockdown panel. Tech check (Hard) seals the main door. This can SAVE the crew from reinforcements coming in from the concourse — or TRAP them in with whatever is already in the hangar. Hard tradeoff worth offering explicitly.

PATROL GEOMETRY: Port Fighter Line and Starboard Fighter Line cross-fire the open floor. Taking cover in the port line means losing sightlines to the starboard line and vice-versa. Crew either splits the room or commits to one side.

EXIT VECTOR: s4 (Grand Theft Starship) begins the moment a PC reaches a Z-95 cockpit and powers up. If the hangar bay doors are sealed by the lockdown panel, a PC must also hit the external bay-door control (another Tech beat) before liftoff.

scenes.title: Skirmish Over Bespin
scenes.readAloud:
You break atmosphere and the sensor board lights up. The Imperial Star Destroyer Assiduous hangs in high orbit, launching TIE Fighters. The Shackles of Nizon — a transport filled with slaves — drifts dead in space. A massive automated Tibanna Gas Hauler is burning hard on a collision course with the slave ship.

Varth's voice crackles from the Banshee, cold and professional:

"Good work getting airborne. That Gas Hauler is going to impact the transport in less than two minutes. It's a tragedy, but it's not our tragedy. We have the credits, we have the data. Spool up the hyperdrives. Let's get out of here while we're rich."

Then a frantic transmission cuts through:

"Varth! I'm on the transport! The slave circuits are locked! I can't steer and sensors show collision imminent! Where is that backup code?!"

It's Maya.
scenes.gmNotes:
The moral climax of Act I. Maya went to the Shackles of Nizon on her own — she couldn't let the slaves die after Varth refused to help. Varth knew she went and deliberately did not tell the crew. He's aboard the Banshee, safely out of the blast zone. The Empire is using the Gas Hauler as a ram to destroy the Shackles of Nizon. Varth's position: 'She made her choice. We jump. Now.' The heroes must choose: follow Varth and leave Maya to die, or turn and fight. If they fight, they engage TIE Fighters to destroy the Gas Hauler. Varth eventually helps — not from altruism, but because he needs the heroes alive for the fortune.

decisionPoints.prompt: Do the heroes turn back to save Maya and the Shackles of Nizon?

options.label: Turn and fight to save Maya
options.consequence: Heroes engage TIEs and destroy the Gas Hauler. Maya survives. Varth reluctantly helps. Heroic but dangerous.

effect.masterful: You defy Varth. Your ship, your choice. No hesitation. Maya lives.
effect.legendary: You don't just defy Varth — you redefine the mission. 'We're not the kind of people who leave someone to die.' The crew follows your lead. Varth is silent.

scenes.title: The Choice
scenes.subtitle: End of Act I
scenes.readAloud:
The Tibanna Gas Hauler explodes in a massive fireball just meters from the slave ship. Maya's voice cuts through the static, shaking with relief: "Slave circuits fried. I have helm control. Jumping to Takodana."

The Assiduous opens fire with turbolasers. Green bolts flash past your cockpit. Varth screams from the Banshee:

"We overstayed our welcome! PUNCH IT!"

The stars stretch into lines and you're gone.

You drop out of hyperspace over Takodana. Green forests and silver lakes fill the viewport below — and hanging in low orbit, engines dark, is the Shackles of Nizon. A massive Imperial bulk transport, its hull scarred and ugly, cargo bays built for three hundred bodies in chains. The slave circuits are dark. The running lights are on.

Maya got here first.
scenes.gmNotes:
The aftermath of Act I. The crew arrives at Takodana to find the Shackles of Nizon already in orbit — Maya jumped here ahead of them. The bulk transport is too large to land; it sits in low orbit while Maya shuttles freed slaves down to Maz Kanata's castle. Denia is already planetside — she's been recovering at Maz's since the end of Adventure 2. The Banshee is docked at the castle.

When the crew lands at Maz's castle, Maya is waiting. She walks straight to Varth and punches him in the jaw. He takes it. 'She made her choice. And you made yours.' Varth doesn't apologize — he never does.

Rewards: The Glorious Chariot, Z-95 fighters, tournament winnings, Varga's assets, Project Leviathan files. Varth unlocks the encrypted account and pays the crew their cut.

Varth's pivot: 'This data points to a massive construction project in the Unknown Regions. If you want to know what the Empire is really building, we have to go off the map.' He looks at Denia: 'How did the Jedi navigate this part of space?' Denia suggests the Ebon Spire on the forest moon of Endor. Varth nods like he's hearing it for the first time.

This concludes Act I and sets up the campaign's second act. Takodana — Maz's castle — is the crew's home base.

[OUTCOME B — VARTH RECOLOR.] Under Outcome B (Dirty Money fork won at adv3-p2-s4), Maya never went to the Shackles of Nizon on her own — because the Shackles lead never surfaced. Varth's deception in this scene is recolored: he is not concealing what he allowed to happen to Maya at the slave transport, he is concealing the simpler, drier truth that he was prepared to let it happen if the lead had materialized. Maya is alive and on the Banshee. The moral weight of this scene shifts from "what Varth let Maya die for" to "what Varth was willing to let her die for." Same fracture, different evidence in hand.

disciplineChallenges.context: Jumping to hyperspace under turbolaser fire.

control.failure: Glancing turbolaser hit during jump. Ship takes damage but enters hyperspace. Repairs needed.
control.mastery: Clean jump AND you enter hyperspace on a vector that makes pursuit impossible — the Star Destroyer can't follow without recalculating. Total escape.

effect.fleeting: Hull shudders from a near-miss. The navicomputer locks and you punch it. Stars stretch — but the ship groans.
effect.masterful: Clean jump. Stars stretch into lines. The turbolaser fire flashes harmlessly behind you.
effect.legendary: Perfect microjump timing. You enter hyperspace in the exact gap between turbolaser salvos. Not a scratch on the hull. Textbook.

disciplineChallenges.context: Reading Varth after his silence nearly killed Maya. What is he really?

control.failure: His explanation seems reasonable — 'tactical calculation.' But something doesn't sit right. You can't articulate why.
control.mastery: You see through everything. Varth isn't just calculating — he's rehearsed. He expected this confrontation and prepared responses. He's been managing you from the beginning.

effect.fleeting: Cold. He's processing, not feeling. The mathematical precision of his response is unsettling.
effect.masterful: Cold. Calculating. He didn't hesitate to sacrifice her. He will do it again if the math works. This is who he is.
effect.legendary: Complete psychological profile: Varth views people as assets to be deployed and expended. His charm is a tool. His loyalty is conditional. Every relationship is a transaction — including this one.

disciplineChallenges.context: Confronting Varth about knowing Maya was on the slave ship and saying nothing.

control.failure: Varth deflects cleanly. 'Tactical calculation that changed. You made a different call. I respect that.' Smooth as durasteel.
control.mastery: Varth drops the mask entirely. A flash of genuine emotion — not remorse, but frustration. 'You don't understand what's at stake.' He almost says too much. Almost reveals the bigger picture.

effect.fleeting: Varth pauses. Considers your words. Then: 'Noted.' That's all you get. The wall is up.
effect.masterful: Varth drops the mask for a moment. 'I did what I thought was necessary. I was wrong.' Genuine or calculated? Hard to tell — but the crack is real.
effect.legendary: Varth is genuinely shaken. For one unguarded moment, you see the real man behind the Admiral's bearing — someone who knows he's becoming something he despises. The moment passes. But you saw it.

disciplineChallenges.context: Processing the emotional weight of Act I's events.

control.failure: [Rattled] carries into the next adventure. The weight lingers. Sleepless nights.
control.mastery: Not just processing — transforming. The events of Bespin forge a harder, clearer version of yourself. Begin the next adventure with renewed purpose.

effect.fleeting: You compartmentalize. File it away. Not healthy, but functional. You can operate.
effect.masterful: Steel yourself. Ready for whatever comes next. The experiences of Act I have made you stronger.
effect.legendary: Clarity. Everything that happened — Raden's death, Maya's rescue, Varth's mask slipping — it all resolves into purpose. You know what you're fighting for now. Nothing can shake that.
